title: LB Omnichord kit-independent drum activity timing catalogue — Gamma9001 musical refresh

repository_contract.design_status: canonical runtime activity catalogue; Gamma9001 quality refresh 2026-09-05
repository_contract.refresh_intent: Rewrite all 54 activity grooves so level 1 is already musically usable and levels 4-5 exploit the existing logical-role palette more fully. Gamma9001 is the musical quality reference; Tiny and General MIDI remain compatible realizations through the existing role resolver.

design_contract.dedicated_fill_rule: No periodic/autonomous drum fill is embedded in activity level 5; explicit intermezzos live in drum_fills_timing.json.
design_contract.kit_independence: Events contain only tick, logical_role and velocity. Concrete samples/presets/MIDI notes live in kit-specific instrument files.
design_contract.amy_48ppq_rule: All ticks are even and therefore exactly convertible from 96 PPQ to AMY 48 PPQ by integer division by two.
design_contract.tag_capacity_target: Every complete activity pattern requires <=56 percussion onset tags under the current percussion lane capacity.
design_contract.authoring_principle: Use established genre drum/percussion idioms, not arbitrary novelty. Upper activity levels add syncopation, ghost notes, cymbal/ride detail, hand percussion or tonal color while remaining a stable repeating accompaniment.
design_contract.cycle_length_policy: A repeating groove may use a one-bar period when musically complete, avoiding duplicated identical onsets used only to fill an older two-bar storage period. This preserves richer complete activity levels within the 56-event sequencer limit; fills remain separate.
design_contract.execution_headroom_policy: Genre color must not consume AMY sequence-execution reserve. Merengue retains its richer timing but is bounded to six Latin logical functions so the established worst-case 34-of-40 execution characterization remains intact.

logical_roles.low_primary: Primary low-frequency pulse/anchor; usually a bass drum but kit mapping owns the sound.
logical_roles.section_accent: Strong bright accent marking a structural point; not a mandatory crash sample.
logical_roles.timeline_primary: Clave/bell/timeline function for styles whose identity needs a repeating timeline.
logical_roles.hand_accent: Hand/electronic accent function such as clap/cowbell depending on kit/style.
logical_roles.electronic_detail: Short synthetic/electronic detail or stutter function.

level_semantics.name: foundation
level_semantics.meaning: A restrained but complete, immediately usable groove. It must carry the meter and the style identity without relying on later activity levels.

level_semantics.name: core groove
level_semantics.meaning: Adds characteristic secondary pulse, offbeat or subdivision relationships while preserving the complete level-1 groove.

level_semantics.name: normal
level_semantics.meaning: Normal accompaniment density with the genre's usual timekeeper, ghost or supporting motion.

level_semantics.name: active
level_semantics.meaning: Adds style-appropriate pickups, open/foot hats, bells, hand percussion, rim detail or secondary accents.

level_semantics.name: maximum activity
level_semantics.meaning: Adds controlled tonal, ghost, cymbal or electronic color while remaining a repeating groove; never an autonomous fill.

musical_basis.method: Original LB-authored accompaniment patterns built from standard, widely used genre conventions rather than copied drum transcriptions.
conventions: Pop, rock, punk, metal and soul use the conventional kick/backbeat relationship with quarter-, eighth- or sixteenth-note timekeeping appropriate to density.
Shuffle, blues and jazz swing use triplet/swing subdivision; jazz favors ride/sustain timekeeping with foot closure and light comping rather than a rock backbeat.
Disco, house, techno and trance use four-on-the-floor foundations with backbeat/clap and offbeat/open-hat development.

Hip-hop and boom-bap use syncopated kick plus beats-2-and-4 backbeat; dubstep and trap use common half-time backbeat organization, with trap adding controlled fast hat/electronic detail only at higher activity.

Bossa nova, samba, salsa, cha-cha, mambo, merengue, cumbia, bolero and Afro-Cuban patterns use timeline, shaker and hand-percussion relationships appropriate to those families; 3-2 son/rumba clave IDs retain explicit two-bar clave timelines.
Reggae level 1 is a one-drop-oriented complete groove; higher levels add restrained steppers/rockers color without replacing the basic identity.
Odd meters are grouped explicitly: 5/4 as 3+2 quarter-note groups, 7/8 as 2+2+3 eighth-note groups, 9/8 as 2+2+2+3, 11/8 as 3+3+3+2, and 7/4 funk as 4+3.
musical_basis.non_goal: Activity level 5 is not a fill. Structural fills remain exclusively in drum_fills_timing.json.
